{{Quote|I ''do'' know some of your secrets. The tomb on Korriban in which this holocron was found was not the ''real'' tomb of Darth Andeddu. That much my research shows me. If it were found&hellip;if Darth Andeddu reawoke&hellip;''"<br />"''Would that make you worthy? Perhaps&mdash;if you survive the journey.|Darth Wyyrlok and the gatekeeper of Darth Andeddu's holocron|<ref name="leg27" />}}
A '''mission to Prakith''' was undertaken in [[137 ABY]] by the [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Darth Wyyrlok (III)|Darth Wyyrlok III]], [[Regent/Legends|chief lieutenant]] of [[Darth Krayt]]'s [[One Sith]] Order. The necessity of the mission was born out of a need by Wyyrlok's [[Sith Master/Legends|Master]], Krayt, to rid himself of the [[Yuuzhan Vong]] [[Yorik-Kul|implants]] that were threatening to [[Death/Legends|end]] his life. After tirelessly researching ancient [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] secrets for answers, Wyyrlok consulted a [[Sith holocron/Legends|Sith holocron]] in his possession, [[Holocron of Heresies|that]] of the long deceased [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord]] [[Darth Andeddu]], who was known to have preserved his [[Force ghost/Legends|essence]] for a time after his own death. Wyyrlok then traveled to the [[Deep Core/Legends|Deep Core]] to Andeddu's [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] of [[Prakith/Legends|Prakith]], searching for information that would assist Krayt.

Wyyrlok managed to find [[Andeddu's Keep]], where he encountered a previously unknown [[Sith cult/Legends|Sith cult]] called the [[Malevolence (cult)|Malevolence]]&mdash;one that worshiped Andeddu, and also refused to allow Wyyrlok further entry into their domain. Wyyrlok would not be denied, however, and he killed all the cultists save one named [[Gerlun]], who revived Andeddu's deceased corpse at the cost of his own life. Andeddu then engaged Wyyrlok in a duel of [[The Force/Legends|Force]] [[Force power/Legends|abilities]], a battle that Andeddu ultimately lost. With the ancient Sith [[Lord/Legends|Lord]] dead for a second time, Wyyrlok returned Andeddu's body to its sarcophagus and sealed it within.

Wyyrlok's mission was partially unsuccessful, as he was still unable to obtain any information in Andeddu's vast collection of Sith lore that would help him in the preservation of Krayt's life. He did, however, recognize what was truly killing the Dark Lord&mdash;his own doubts that he would not survive to see his dream of a stable [[The galaxy/Legends|galaxy]] under Sith rule fulfilled.

==Prelude==
{{Quote|We require knowledge only ''you'' possess. You animated your own body after death. Your mind functioned. Your body responded to its commands. We require that knowledge and you, a holocron, are obliged to give it.''"<br />"''Obliged? I am ''obliged'' to share my knowledge ''only'' with those Sith wise enough, powerful enough, to command it. You desire my secrets to preserve the life of that pretender.|Darth Wyyrlok and Darth Andeddu's holocron|<ref name="leg27" />}}
[[File:KeepInside1.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Darth Wyyrlok explores the interior of Andeddu's Keep.]]
Decades before the end of the [[Sith–Imperial War]] and the onset of the [[Second Imperial Civil War]], [[Darth Krayt|A'Sharad Hett]], who would become [[Darth/Legends|Darth]] Krayt, [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]], had been captured by the [[Unknown Regions/Legends|extra]]-[[The galaxy/Legends|galactic]] [[Yuuzhan Vong]] [[Species/Legends|species]] and implanted with their [[Yorik-Kul]] slave seeds. Though able to combat the effects of the seeds through his growing strength in the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side of the Force]], Hett was slowly losing his battle with them. By [[137 ABY]], he had assumed the mantle of Dark Lord and restyled himself as the [[Dragon]] of the Sith, but the coral seeds still threatened to turn him into a mindless shell of a [[Gender/Legends|man]].<ref name="leg17">[[Legacy (2006) 17|''Legacy'' (2006) 17]]</ref>

For years Krayt was able to sustain himself through [[Force healing/Legends|healing trances]] and extended periods of [[Force Stasis/Legends|stasis]], and he was looked after by the most trusted of his servants, the latest of them being [[Darth Wyyrlok (III)|Darth Wyyrlok the third]]. Despite being the most learned of Krayt's [[One Sith|Order]] in [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] lore and ritual, Wyyrlok was unable to find a way to cure that which afflicted his [[Sith Master/Legends|Master]]. Thus, he consulted a [[Sith holocron/Legends|holocron]] in his possession, one that belonged to an ancient [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] named [[Darth Andeddu]], who was known to have reanimated his flesh after his own [[Death/Legends|death]]. The [[Gatekeeper/Legends|gatekeeper]] of [[Holocron of Heresies|Andeddu's holocron]] refused to reveal its secrets to save Krayt, whom it considered a pretender to the Sith legacy. Only after Wyyrlok alluded to actually reviving Andeddu's body did the gatekeeper reveal the location of [[Andeddu's Keep]], on his [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] of [[Prakith/Legends|Prakith]]. Wyyrlok immediately set out in his [[Fury-class starfighter|personal fighter]] to the [[Deep Core/Legends|Deep Core]], in search of Andeddu's domain and his coveted life-sustaining abilities.<ref name="leg27" />

==The mission==
===Arrival on Prakith===
{{Quote|Intruder! Intruder! Intruder! Intruder!|Voices of the Malevolence cultists, as Wyyrlok enters Andeddu's Keep|<ref name="leg27" />}}
Once arriving on Prakith with Andeddu's holocron, Wyyrlok entered the dilapidated fortress of Darth Andeddu, and was soon confronted by members of the [[Malevolence (cult)|Malevolence cult]], guardians of Andeddu's tomb. Refusing to allow Wyyrlok to pass, they approached him with ignited [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsabers]], intent on killing him. However, Wyyrlok displayed his proficiency with [[Sith sorcery/Legends|Sith sorcery]], using [[Mind trick/Legends|illusions]] to trick the cultists into killing each other. All perished except for one, [[Gerlun]], who swore fealty to Wyyrlok and led him to Andeddu's tomb. With Andeddu's holocron in hand, Wyyrlok was instructed by its gatekeeper to place the holocron on Andeddu's body to revive him, and thus learn all his secrets. Wyyrlok refused and was instead content with simply learning what he could from Andeddu's vast collection of [[Sith spellbook/Legends|books]] and [[Sith scroll/Legends|scrolls]]. In an attempt to avenge himself on Wyyrlok for defeating his fellow cultists earlier, Gerlun used [[The Force/Legends|the Force]] [[Telekinesis/Legends|to grab]] the holocron and placed it on Andeddu's body, and to both of their surprise, the holocron's power was burned out, as Gerlun's own life force was drained to restore Andeddu's life.<ref name="leg27" />

===Confrontation with Andeddu===
[[File:Leg27-DuelonPrakith.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Darth Wyyrlok battles Darth Andeddu with Sith sorcery.]]
{{Quote|Knowledge is ''power'' and true Sith do not ''share'' power. I will give you nothing but your own death.''"<br />"''I know about ''power''.''"<br />"''Very well, whelp. We shall duel&mdash;but on a field of ''my'' choosing!|Darths Andeddu and Wyyrlok|<ref name="leg27" />}}
Although Andeddu had been revived, he refused to share his knowledge with Wyyrlok, stating that he believed that true Sith did not share power. He then attacked Wyyrlok with a barrage of [[Force lightning/Legends|Sith lightning]], but Wyyrlok [[Tutaminis|absorbed]] it in the palm of his hand. Andeddu challenged Wyyrlok to a duel of Force abilities, immediately Force-pushing him away while creating illusions of massive rocks, which he then hurled at Wyyrlok.<ref name="leg27" />

Wyyrlok was not so easily bested, and he quickly saw through Andeddu's tricks. He realized that Andeddu had a fear of death, and he took control of Andeddu's illusions of lava and flames to seemingly destroy all of Andeddu's books and scrolls. Mortified by the destruction of his precious [[Sith artifact/Legends|artifacts]], Andeddu believed Wyyrlok's illusion to be real even as Wyyrlok turned the lava and flames against his opponent. Andeddu perished a second time, consumed by his own fears of dying.<ref name="leg27" />

Wyyrlok placed Andeddu's soulless body back into its tomb and proceeded to study much of the lore in Andeddu's collection. However, nothing that Wyyrlok found in Andeddu's Keep spoke of any way to heal or preserve life through the dark side of the Force. What Wyyrlok did realize was that more than just physical affliction was killing Darth Krayt&mdash;his doubts of living long enough to ensure stability in [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] were having an equal effect on him as were the Vong slave seeds. Taking several books and scrolls, Wyyrlok left the keep and returned to his Master, even more determined to find another way to heal him.<ref name="leg27" />

==Aftermath==
{{Quote|I created the One Sith to impose order on chaos and unite the galaxy under my rule. But I feel my order&mdash;my ''vision''&mdash;will not survive my death.|Darth Krayt, doubting his survival|<ref name="leg30">[[Legacy (2006) 30|''Legacy'' (2006) 30]]</ref>}}
[[File:WyyrlokKraytConcerned.jpg|thumb|left|220px|Darth Wyyrlok discusses Karness Muur's healing abilities with Darth Krayt.]]
Eventually, Krayt did uncover a way to finally rid himself of the seeds<ref name="leg31">[[Legacy (2006) 31|''Legacy'' (2006) 31]]</ref> but was unable to make full use of the power. Sometime after Wyyrlok's mission to Prakith, Krayt was lured into a trap by the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] and [[Imperial Knight]]s of the [[Fel Empire]], where he briefly subjected himself to the healing powers of the ancient Sith spirit of [[Karness Muur]], who was using [[Celeste Morne|one of the Jedi]] as a host body. When the [[Battle on Had Abbadon|trap]] was sprung,<ref name="leg30" /> Krayt was mortally wounded by one of the Imperials, shortly after figuring out how Muur was killing the slave seeds. When Wyyrlok found him to be alive, Krayt requested that Wyyrlok place him in a [[Bacta tank/Legends|bacta tank]] so that his current wounds could be healed while he grew strong enough to complete the purging process that Muur had started.<ref name="leg31" /> Instead, Wyyrlok enacted one of the core philosophies of the Sith<ref name="RoTSn">[[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith (novelization)|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'' novelization]]</ref> and betrayed his Master by murdering him.<ref name="leg31" />

==Behind the scenes==
The mission to Prakith first appeared in the twenty-seventh issue of the ''[[Star Wars: Legacy]]'' [[Star Wars comic books|comic]] series titled [[Legacy (2006) 27|''Into the Core'']], by writer [[John Ostrander]]. Ostrander uses this mission to expand somewhat on the backstory of Darth Andeddu by introducing both his homeworld and the Malevolence cult. Ostrander reveals here that it is not just the Yuuzhan Vong implants that threaten Darth Krayt's life, but that his doubts and fears play into his failing condition as well.
